title: Everest Base Camp Trek
summary: The classic Khumbu trail to Everest Base Camp, paced for acclimatization with Sherpa-led guiding from Kathmandu.
overview: Everest Base Camp is the journey most travelers picture when they think of Nepal: prayer flags, stone villages, and a trail that climbs from rhododendron forest into the high Khumbu. World Touch runs this trek from our Kathmandu office, so flights, permits, and lodge bookings are handled before you ever reach Lukla.

Days are built around altitude, not speed. You walk with a licensed guide, sleep in teahouses, and keep rest days at Namche and Dingboche. The reward is Kala Patthar at sunrise and Base Camp itself — a place that still feels earned.
This departure suits fit walkers who are new to high altitude and want a trusted local team rather than a last-minute package.

faqs.question: How fit do I need to be for Everest Base Camp?
faqs.answer: You should be comfortable walking 5–7 hours a day on uneven trails. Prior high-altitude experience is helpful but not required if you follow the acclimatization plan.

faqs.question: What is the best season?
faqs.answer: Spring (March–May) and autumn (September–November) offer the most stable weather and clear mountain views.

title: Annapurna Circuit Trek
summary: A full circuit of the Annapurna massif, crossing Thorong La and descending into the Kali Gandaki.
overview: The Annapurna Circuit is Nepal’s great traverse: rice terraces, apple orchards, high desert, and one serious pass. It rewards travelers who want variety more than a single viewpoint.
We start after a road transfer from Kathmandu or Pokhara and keep the walking days human. Thorong La is attempted only after proper acclimatization in Manang.
Finish in the Kali Gandaki and continue to Pokhara — an easy link to our daily tourist bus if you are heading back to Kathmandu.

title: Annapurna Base Camp Trek
summary: A shorter Annapurna classic into the sanctuary, with Poon Hill sunrise on the way.
overview: Annapurna Base Camp is the right trek if you want a high Himalayan amphitheater without a 5,000-meter pass. The trail climbs through Gurung villages into the Annapurna Sanctuary.
Most itineraries include a Poon Hill sunrise before or after the sanctuary. We usually pair this trek with a night in Pokhara and a seat on our Kathmandu–Pokhara bus.

title: Langtang Valley Trek
summary: A week in the valley north of Kathmandu — glaciers, Tamang villages, and no domestic flight.
overview: Langtang is the trek we recommend when you want mountains without a Lukla flight. A road transfer from Kathmandu reaches the trail in a morning, and you are in a high valley within a few days.
Kyanjin Gompa is the heart of the route, with optional day hikes toward Tserko Ri if the weather is kind.

title: Ghorepani Poon Hill Trek
summary: A short Annapurna classic for sunrise over Dhaulagiri and Annapurna from Poon Hill.
overview: Poon Hill is the introduction we suggest for families and first-time trekkers. The walking is steady, the villages are lively, and the sunrise is the reason people come back to Nepal for longer routes.
Combine it with Pokhara and the daily bus so the whole trip stays simple.

faqs.question: Is Poon Hill suitable for beginners?
faqs.answer: Yes. It is the most approachable overnight trek we run, as long as you are fine with stone steps.

title: Mardi Himal Trek
summary: A quieter ridge trek with close views of Machhapuchhre, based from Pokhara.
overview: Mardi Himal sits just off the classic Annapurna routes, which keeps the trail quieter. The ridge walk toward High Camp is the highlight — Fishtail fills the sky.
It is a strong choice if you have a week and want something more alpine than Poon Hill.

title: Manaslu Circuit Trek
summary: A restricted-area circuit around Manaslu for trekkers who want fewer crowds than Annapurna.
overview: Manaslu is the circuit people choose after they have seen the classic trails. It requires a restricted-area permit and a licensed guide — both of which we arrange in Kathmandu before departure.
The trail follows the Budhi Gandaki, crosses Larke La, and finishes toward the Annapurna side. Expect long days and a genuine sense of remoteness.

title: Gokyo Lakes Trek
summary: Turquoise lakes and a Gokyo Ri panorama — the quieter side of the Khumbu.
overview: Gokyo is for travelers who want Everest-region scale without the Base Camp crowds. The lakes sit under Cho Oyu, and Gokyo Ri gives one of the widest panoramas in Nepal.
We can extend toward Everest Base Camp via Cho La if you have extra days and good weather.

title: Upper Mustang Trek
summary: Walled Lo Manthang and a high desert kingdom north of the Annapurnas.
overview: Upper Mustang feels unlike the rest of Nepal: red cliffs, cave dwellings, and a Tibetan-influenced culture in Lo Manthang. It is a restricted region, so permits are a real part of the planning — we handle them in Kathmandu.
Walking is on dry trails rather than forest. The season is narrower, and the permit cost is higher than standard treks, which is reflected in the price.

title: Everest Three Passes Trek
summary: Kongma La, Cho La, and Renjo La — the full Khumbu for experienced trekkers.
overview: Three Passes is the Khumbu without shortcuts. You link Everest Base Camp, the Gokyo lakes, and three high passes. It is for people who have trekked before and want a longer, harder route.
We keep group sizes small and build weather days into the plan so a closed pass does not wreck the trip.
